newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain government hopes Italy can enter EMU on time.
newsitem.headline: Spain government hopes Italy can enter EMU on time.

text.p: Spanish Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro denied on Wednesday any possible conspiracy directed against the Italian lira and said he hoped Italy can enter the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) on time.

Speaking on Spanish television, Montoro said Italy's inclusion in the single currency was important, adding "far from a plot against (Italy), the only plots there should be are positive ones. The large European countries should be on time (for EMU). None should be missing."
The larger the number of countries from the start of the project, the better, he said.

The Spanish daily "El Mundo" said on Wednesday that Italy criticised Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and French President Jacques Chirac and claimed there was a "plot" directed against the lira.
This followed a joint interview published on Monday by the Financial Times and Expansion in which Aznar said Italy wanted the two countries to "walk together holding hands towards Maastricht."

"In Spain, a very large mayority thinks it is important to enter EMU on time so we have to do everything needed to be sure Spain will enter according to the planned timetable, and what I think is also important is that Italy will be there too," Montoro said.
